name: Rahil Ehtesham Mehr
interests: Perovskite solar cells and thin-film photovoltaics
bio: I'm a physics undergraduate at Sharif University of Technology working in experimental condensed matter physics. What draws me to the field is the link between how a material is made and what it can do: how growth, interfaces, and thickness, down to a single atomic layer, determine its properties and its potential in devices.

My research follows two directions. In photovoltaics, I fabricate perovskite solar cells at the Nanoparticles and Coatings Lab (NCL), working hands-on with solution-based thin-film deposition, where small changes in processing show up directly in film quality and device performance. In two-dimensional materials, I work on a gold-assisted exfoliation method that uses the strong Au–chalcogen bond to separate large-area, single-crystal monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides. The aim is to move from microscopic flakes toward macroscopic samples suitable for quantum materials and device research.

I also have a computational background in biomedical optics, where I modeled laser–tissue interactions and simulated photon transport in multilayer skin. Combining modeling with fabrication and characterization shapes how I design and interpret experiments. More about my research, teaching, and background is in my CV.
personal: Beyond physics, I’m a [FIDE-rated chess player][fide-profile], a member of Sharif’s university chess team, and a certified chess instructor. I taught at Shahmate chess school from March 2023 to July 2026. Competitive chess has shaped my analytical thinking, strategic decision-making, and approach to complex problems. I also organize university tournaments and contribute chess puzzles to the university newspaper. Away from the board, I enjoy running, skating, karate, cinema, and tea.
highlight: I am looking for graduate positions in experimental condensed matter physics, starting in 2027.
